ADJOURNED

  MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JANUARY 18, 2017

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 5:40 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

3.  ITEM FOR DISCUSSION

A.  PHASE I STUDY: REVIEW OF SALARY ADMINISTRATION POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the recommendations set forth
  by Jan Perkins, Senior Partner, Management Partners.

  Jan Perkins, Senior Partner, provided an extensive presentation (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Mrs. Perkins noted that there are a
  number of factors, including demographic and economic, that are making it
  difficult for cities to recruit qualified candidates, thus making the market very
  competitive.

  City Manager Prichard noted that all cities are having a difficult time finding
  candidates, especially for mid-career professional positions.

  Mrs. Perkins noted that entry level employees of the millennial generation are
  seeking opportunities to develop and learn to advance their career positions and
  salaries and are less interested in long term service to one organization. She
  also noted that it is usually more cost effective to reward existing employees
  than to deal with the costs associated with turnover.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that many of his students are interested in non-
  profit organizations rather than cities.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Mrs. Perkins noted that merit pay
  systems are performance-based, and are considered a best management
  practice, while step-based pay systems reward time in service. She indicated
  that the purpose behind Cost of Living Adjustments (COLA) is to ensure that
  the “buying power” of the employee is not eroded over time.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN stated that retention of employees may not need to
  be considered as heavily because many of the current employees have been
  with the City for 15 years or more.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ disagreed noting that some employees will be
  retiring soon and retention should be definitely be considered. City Manager
  Prichard noted that one of the reasons employees have stayed for so long is that
  they have been paid fairly.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JANUARY 18, 2017
   COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN indicated his satisfaction with the recent practice
  of granting the City Manager discretion over a defined pool of funds to be used
  for merit based rewards.

  City Manager Prichard explained the merit system which the City utilized prior
  to 2008, detailing the COUNCIL’S involvement in setting the standard salary
  award percentage and the method by which the City Manager could make
  awards in excess of that standard percentage for exceptional performance.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ suggested that when a new COUNCIL MEMBER is
  elected, part of the training process should include education on management
  and human resources of the City.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN referred to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and its
  consideration in setting any COLA. He suggested that when it is considered by
  COUNCIL it should be measured from that month closest as practical to the
  beginning of each fiscal year.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ cautioned that the COLA and merit base system
  are two different issues and not to confuse the two.

  City Manager Prichard noted that the COUNCIL has historically considered CPI,
  the City’s fiscal position and its place in the market among other factors to set
  the standard award percentage.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that CPI and other factors should be considered
  instructive, but not determinative.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to consider
  changes in the CPI from April to April as the most useful measurement for
  consideration.

  City Manager Prichard noted that staff will present a Salary Administration and
  Implementation Policy to the COUNCIL at a future meeting.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO PREPARE A MERIT SYSTEM SALARY
  ADMINISTRATION POLICY AND IMPLEMENTATION MEASURES TO
  BRING BACK FOR COUNCIL REVIEW AND APPROVAL.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that it is good to know what other cities are doing
  because the marketplace cannot be ignored.

  City Manager Prichard noted that as part of the implementation of the policy
  goals, he would expect COUNCIL to authorize Phase II of the study for
  Management Partners to undertake a salary survey at this time and every five
  years thereafter. Ms. Perkins indicated that Management Partners would
  suggest comparator cities for COUNCIL to review.

4.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF DECEMBER 13, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF DECEMBER 13, 2016
  AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JANUARY 18, 2017
 B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – DECEMBER AND JANUARY

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57838 THROUGH 57866 IN THE AMOUNT OF

  122816; 57715 THROUGH 57727; 57736 (VOID); 57764 THROUGH
  57832; 57769 (VOID); 57779 (VOID) IN THE AMOUNT OF $764,881.16
  FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $911,854.79 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  NOVEMBER 2016 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

6.  NEW BUSINESS

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 19, 2016

ADJOURNED TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION CORPORATION MEETING AT 6:55 P.M.
****************************************************************************************************

  MEETING

  Recommendation: That the Pepper Tree Foundation Board of Directors: 1)
  Conduct any necessary Foundation business; and 2) Receive and file the staff
  report.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 18, 2017
   COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE REGULAR ANNUAL PEPPER TREE
  FOUNDATION BOARD OF DIRECTORS STAFF REPORT.

  THERE  BEING  NO  OBJECTION,  MAYOR  ZERUNYAN  SO  ORDERED.

D.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD ACTION ITEM FROM
  MEETING OF DECEMBER 19, 2016 – HORSE TRAILER DONATION

  Recommendation:  That the Pepper Tree Foundation Advisory Board of
  Directors donate the former Equestrian Trails Incorporated Corral #8 Horse
  Trailer and its contents to the Peninsula Equestrian Circuit Organization.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO APPROVE DONATING THE FORMER EQUESTRIAN TRAILS
  INCORPORATED CORRAL #8 HORSE TRAILER AND ITS CONTENTS TO
  THE PENINSULA EQUESTRIAN CIRCUIT ORGANIZATION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that since the City’s 60th anniversary of incorporation
  is this year, he proposed that the newly constructed Rolling Hills Country Club
  might be interested in organizing a Mayor’s Golf Tournament, along with the
  USC Golf Team, and that the proceeds could go to the Pepper Tree Foundation
  and USC. He further noted that he will contact the Rolling Hills Country Club
  to see if this event might be possible.

************************************************************************************************
RECONVENED CITY COUNCIL MEETING AT 7:14 P.M.
************************************************************************************************

E.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the items listed and make any
  additions or deletions.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL made several suggestions for discussion that
  included solar panels, improved communication with commercial district
  representatives, and installation of fiber optic cable throughout the commercial
  district.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN reported that he attended a meeting with Jonathan Alpert,
  The Promenade, and Planning Director Wahba. He then noted that he would
  like the COUNCIL to discuss the entitlements that were approved for various
  projects in the commercial district as he believed the property owners need to
  hear the COUNCIL’S concerns.

  Planning Director noted that he will update the COUNCIL on major projects at
  the Policy Development Session.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL then suggested discussing the Community Room
  at the corner of Palos Verdes Drive East/Palos Verdes Drive North and the
  undeveloped park site on the northeast corner.

  City Manager Prichard noted that the Park and Activities already has a
  preliminary design for that site and will be provided at the Policy Development
  Session.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that he would like to see that corner property
  rezoned and possibly incorporate a small café that would accommodate walkers
  and those who live in the area.
ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 18, 2017
   City Manager Prichard then mentioned that discussion might also include the
  City’s mission, vision and values and how to create a statement reflective of the
  City’s organizational operations.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that it would be beneficial to provide an
  orientation to new City representatives and staff on how to conduct themselves
  when dealing with the public and each other.

  Planning Director Wahba then provided an update on the Brickwalk Project.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, City Manager Prichard stated that
  a request to authorize solicitation of bids for the City Hall Remodel Project will
  be presented at the next COUNCIL meeting. He further noted that storm drain
  improvement cost estimates will be determined by Sancon, giving the City a
  better understanding of competing capital needs.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that a sample median was reviewed and authorized by the Park and
  Activities Commission, along with input from the Botanic Gardens and
  homeowners’ associations, and was installed in the Hawthorne Boulevard and
  Palos Verdes Drive North median.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING ITEMS FOR
  DISCUSSION:  1)  SOLAR PANELS; 2)  COMMUNICATION WITH
  COMMERCIAL DISTRICT REPRESENTATIVES; 3) CONSIDERATION OF
  THE 50,000 SQUARE FOOT MEDICAL OFFICE CONDITION WITH THE
  PROMENADE; 4)  COMMERCIAL DISTRICT BROADBAND; 5)
  COMMUNITY CENTER POSSIBILITIES; 6) CONSIDERATION OF THE
  UNDEVELOPED PARK AT THE CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST; AND 7)  COUNCIL,
  COMMISSION,  COMMITTEE,  STAFF  ORIENTATION,  MISSION
  STATEMENT AND OPERATIONS.

7.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE POSITIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Reappoint Committee Members
  who have expressed interest in being reappointed; 2) Interview Committee
  Members and applicants and make appointments thereafter; or 3) Continue
  recruitment in hopes of securing more applicants.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that she would like to meet with the current
  Equestrian Committee Members.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO SET UP INTERVIEWS FOR THE FOLLOWING
  INDIVIDUALS: 1) EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEMBERS AND APPLICANT;
  2) TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE APPLICANTS; AND 3) CONTINUE
  TO RECRUIT FOR A PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSIONER.

  City Manager Prichard reported that Senior Planner Naughton has been attending
  the Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) meetings and that it may be time to
  include a COUNCIL MEMBER while negotiations are being undertaken to create a
  Joint Powers Authority (JPA).

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN and COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL volunteered to
  serve on the CCA Committee as delegate and alternate, respectively.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 18, 2017
 8.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:05 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting
  to Tuesday, January 24, 2017 at 5:30 p.m. for the purpose of conducting a first
  look meeting to consider a Peninsula Center boutique hotel.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk
